verses.zh: 到了早晨，众祭司长和民间的长老大家商议要治死耶稣，
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] it was early in the morning, all the chief priests and the elders of the people plotted against Jesus to execute him.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 就把他捆绑，解去，交给巡抚彼拉多。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] tied him up, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate[NOTE:2] the governor.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

Most mss (A C W Γ Δ Θ 0250 ƒ1,13 565 579 700 1241 1424 M latt) have Ποντίῳ (Pontiō, “Pontius”) before Πιλάτῳ (Pilatō, “Pilate”), but there seems to be no reason for omitting the tribal name, either intentionally or unintentionally. Adding “Pontius,” however, is a natural expansion on the text, and is in keeping with several other NT and patristic references to the Roman governor (cf. Luke 3:1; Acts 4:27; 1 Tim 6:13; Ign. Magn. 11.1; Ign. Trall. 9.1; Ign. Smyrn. 1.2; Justin Martyr, passim). See TCGNT 52-53. The shorter reading, supported by א B L 0281 33 co, is thus strongly preferred.

The Jews most assuredly wanted to put Jesus to death, but they lacked the authority to do so. For this reason they handed him over to Pilate in hopes of securing a death sentence. The Romans kept close control of the death penalty in conquered territories to prevent it from being used to execute Roman sympathizers.

verses.zh: 这时候，卖耶稣的犹大看见耶稣已经定了罪，就后悔，把那三十块钱拿回来给祭司长和长老，说：
verses.en: Now when[NOTE:1] Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that Jesus[NOTE:2] had been condemned, he regretted what he had done and returned the 30 silver coins to the chief priests and the elders,
notes: Grk “Then when.” Here τότε (tote) has been translated as “now” to indicate a somewhat parenthetical interlude in the sequence of events.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 「我卖了无辜之人的血是有罪了。」他们说：「那与我们有甚么相干？你自己承当吧！」
verses.en: saying, “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood!” But they said, “What is that to us? You take care of it yourself!”

verses.zh: 犹大就把那银钱丢在殿里，出去吊死了。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] Judas threw the silver coins into the temple and left. Then he went out and hanged himself.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the leaders’ response to Judas.

verses.zh: 祭司长拾起银钱来，说：「这是血价，不可放在库里。」
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] chief priests took the silver and said, “It is not lawful to put this into the temple treasury, since it is blood money.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 他们商议，就用那银钱买了窑户的一块田，为要埋葬外乡人。
verses.en: After[NOTE:1] consulting together they bought the Potter’s Field with it, as a burial place for foreigners.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 所以那块田直到今日还叫做「血田」。
verses.en: For this reason that field has been called the “Field of Blood” to this day.

verses.zh: 这就应了先知耶利米的话，说：「他们用那三十块钱，就是被估定之人的价钱，是以色列人中所估定的，
verses.en: Then what was spoken by Jeremiah[NOTE:1] the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the 30 silver coins, the price of the one whose price had been set by the people of Israel,[NOTE:2]
notes: The problematic citing of Jeremiah for a text which appears to come from Zechariah has prompted certain scribes to alter it. Codex 22 has Ζαχαρίου (Zachariou, “Zechariah”) while Φ 33 and several versional witnesses omit the prophet’s name altogether. And codex 21 and the Latin ms l change the prophet’s name to “Isaiah,” in accordance with natural scribal proclivities to alter the text toward the most prominent OT prophet. But unquestionably the name Jeremiah is the wording of the original here because it is supported by virtually all witnesses and because it is the harder reading. See D. A. Carson, “Matthew,” EBC 8:562-63, for a discussion of the textual and especially hermeneutical problem.
Grk “the sons of Israel,” an idiom referring to the people of Israel as an ethnic entity (L&N 11.58).

verses.zh: 买了窑户的一块田；这是照着主所吩咐我的。」
verses.en: and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord commanded me.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The source of this citation is debated (see the tc note on Jeremiah in v. 9 above for a related discussion). The quotation is most closely related to Zech 11:12-13, but the reference to Jeremiah in v. 9 as the source leads one to look there as well. There is no exact match for this text in Jeremiah, but there are some conceptual parallels: In Jer 18:2-6 the prophet visits a potter, and in Jer 32:6-15 he buys a field. D. A. Carson argues that Jer 19:1-13 is the source of the quotation augmented with various phrases drawn from Zech 11:12-13 (“Matthew,” EBC 8:563). W. D. Davies and D. C. Allison argue that the reference to Jeremiah is not meant to refer to one specific text from that prophet, but instead to signal that his writings as a whole are a source from which the quotation is drawn (Matthew [ICC], 3:568-69). Although the exact source of the citation is uncertain, it is reasonable to see texts from the books of Jeremiah and Zechariah both coming into play here.

verses.zh: 耶稣站在巡抚面前；巡抚问他说：「你是犹太人的王吗？」耶稣说：「你说的是。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him,[NOTE:2] “Are you the king[NOTE:3] of the Jews?” Jesus[NOTE:4] said, “You say so.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “asked him, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
“Are you the king of the Jews?” Pilate was interested in this charge because of its political implications of sedition against Rome.
Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
The reply “You say so” is somewhat enigmatic, like Jesus’ earlier reply to the Jewish leadership in 26:64.

verses.zh: 他被祭司长和长老控告的时候，甚么都不回答。
verses.en: But when he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he did not respond.

verses.zh: 彼拉多就对他说：「他们作见证告你这么多的事，你没有听见吗？」
verses.en: Then Pilate said to him, “Don’t you hear how many charges they are bringing against you?”

verses.zh: 耶稣仍不回答，连一句话也不说，以致巡抚甚觉希奇。
verses.en: But he did not answer even one accusation, so that the governor was quite amazed.

verses.zh: 巡抚有一个常例，每逢这节期，随众人所要的释放一个囚犯给他们。
verses.en: During the feast the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the crowd,[NOTE:1] whomever they wanted.
notes: The custom of Pilate to release one prisoner is unknown outside the gospels in Jewish writings, but it was a Roman custom at the time and thus probably used in Palestine as well (cf. Matt 27:15; John 18:39).

verses.zh: 当时有一个出名的囚犯叫巴拉巴。
verses.en: At that time they had in custody a notorious prisoner named Jesus[NOTE:1] Barabbas.
notes: Although the external evidence for the inclusion of “Jesus” before “Barabbas” (in vv. 16 and 17) is rather sparse, being restricted virtually to mss of what was formally labeled the “Caesarean” text (Θ ƒ1 700* sys arm geo2; Ormss), the omission of the Lord’s name in apposition to “Barabbas” is such a strongly motivated reading that it can hardly be original. There is no good explanation for a scribe unintentionally adding ᾿Ιησοῦν (Iēsoun) before Βαραββᾶν (Barabban), especially since Barabbas is mentioned first in each verse (thus dittography is ruled out). Further, the addition of τὸν λεγόμενον Χριστόν (ton legomenon Christon, “who is called Christ”) to ᾿Ιησοῦν in v. 17 makes better sense if Barabbas is also called “Jesus” (otherwise, a mere “Jesus” would have been a sufficient appellation to distinguish the two). Metzger notes that codex S, a tenth-century majuscule, along with a score of minuscules, have a marginal comment on this verse as follows: “In many ancient copies which I have met with I found Barabbas himself likewise called ‘Jesus.’” The attribution of this scholium is variously given as Anastasius, Chrysostom, or even Origen (TCGNT 56).

verses.zh: 众人聚集的时候，彼拉多就对他们说：「你们要我释放哪一个给你们？是巴拉巴呢？是称为基督的耶稣呢？」
verses.en: So after they had assembled, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release for you, Jesus[NOTE:1] Barabbas or Jesus who is called the Christ?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Again, as in v. 16, the name “Jesus” is supplied before “Barabbas” in Θ ƒ1 700* sys Ormss (Θ 700* lack the article τόν [ton] before Βαραββᾶν [Barabban]). The same argument for accepting the inclusion of “Jesus” as the earlier reading in the previous verse applies here as well.
Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 1:16.

verses.zh: 巡抚原知道他们是因为嫉妒才把他解了来。
verses.en: (For he knew that they had handed him over because of envy.)[NOTE:1]
notes: This is a parenthetical note by the author.

verses.zh: 正坐堂的时候，他的夫人打发人来说：「这义人的事，你一点不可管，因为我今天在梦中为他受了许多的苦。」
verses.en: As[NOTE:1] he was sitting on the judgment seat,[NOTE:2] his wife sent a message[NOTE:3] to him:[NOTE:4] “Have nothing to do with that innocent man;[NOTE:5] I have suffered greatly as a result of a dream[NOTE:6] about him today.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

Or “the judge’s seat.”sn The judgment seat (βῆμα, bēma) was a raised platform mounted by steps and usually furnished with a seat. It was used by officials in addressing an assembly or making official pronouncements, often of a judicial nature.
The word “message” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.
Grk “saying.” The participle λέγουσα (legousa) is redundant here in contemporary English and has not been translated.
The Greek particle γάρ (gar, “for”) has not been translated here.
Or “suffered greatly in a dream.” See the discussion on the construction κατ᾿ ὄναρ (kat’ onar) in BDAG 710 s.v. ὄναρ.

verses.zh: 祭司长和长老挑唆众人，求释放巴拉巴，除灭耶稣。
verses.en: But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus killed.

verses.zh: 巡抚对众人说：「这两个人，你们要我释放哪一个给你们呢？」他们说：「巴拉巴。」
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] governor asked them, “Which of the two do you want me to release for you?” And they said, “Barabbas!”
notes: Grk “answering, the governor said to them.” This construction is somewhat redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 彼拉多说：「这样，那称为基督的耶稣我怎么办他呢？」他们都说：「把他钉十字架！」
verses.en: Pilate said to them, “Then what should I do with Jesus who is called the Christ?”[NOTE:1] They all said, “Crucify him!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 1:16.

Grk “Him—be crucified!” The third person imperative is difficult to translate because English has no corresponding third person form for the imperative. The traditional translation “Let him be crucified” sounds as if the crowd is giving consent or permission. “He must be crucified” is closer, but it is more natural in English to convert the passive to active and simply say “Crucify him.”sn See the note on crucified in 20:19.

verses.zh: 巡抚说：「为甚么呢？他做了甚么恶事呢？」他们便极力地喊着说：「把他钉十字架！」
verses.en: He asked, “Why? What wrong has he done?” But they shouted more insistently, “Crucify him!”

verses.zh: 彼拉多见说也无济于事，反要生乱，就拿水在众人面前洗手，说：「流这义人的血，罪不在我，你们承当吧。」
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] Pilate saw that he could do nothing, but that instead a riot was starting, he took some water, washed his hands before the crowd and said, “I am innocent of this man’s blood. You take care of it yourselves!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
You take care of it yourselves! Compare the response of the chief priests and elders to Judas in 27:4. The expression is identical except that in 27:4 it is singular and here it is plural.

verses.zh: 众人都回答说：「他的血归到我们和我们的子孙身上。」
verses.en: In[NOTE:1] reply all the people said, “Let his blood be on us and on our children!”
notes: Grk “answering, all the people said.” This construction is somewhat redundant in English and has been simplified in the translation.

verses.zh: 于是彼拉多释放巴拉巴给他们，把耶稣鞭打了，交给人钉十字架。
verses.en: Then he released Barabbas for them. But after he had Jesus flogged,[NOTE:1] he handed him over[NOTE:2] to be crucified.[NOTE:3]
notes: A Roman flogging (traditionally, “scourging”) was an excruciating punishment. The victim was stripped of his clothes and bound to a post with his hands fastened above him (or sometimes he was thrown to the ground). Guards standing on either side of the victim would incessantly beat him with a whip (flagellum) made out of leather with pieces of lead and bone inserted into its ends. While the Jews only allowed 39 lashes, the Romans had no such limit; many people who received such a beating died as a result. See C. Schneider, TDNT, 4:515-19.tn The Greek term φραγελλόω (phragelloō) refers to flogging. BDAG 1064 s.v. states, “flog, scourge, a punishment inflicted on slaves and provincials after a sentence of death had been pronounced on them. So in the case of Jesus before the crucifixion…Mt 27:26; Mk 15:15.”
Or “delivered him up.”
See the note on crucified in 20:19.

verses.zh: 巡抚的兵就把耶稣带进衙门，叫全营的兵都聚集在他那里。
verses.en: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the governor’s residence[NOTE:1] and gathered the whole cohort[NOTE:2] around him.
notes: Or “into their headquarters”; Grk “into the praetorium.” sn The governor’s residence (Grk “praetorium”) was the Roman governor’s official residence. The one in Jerusalem may have been Herod’s palace in the western part of the city, or the fortress Antonia northwest of the temple area.
A Roman cohort was a tenth of a legion, about 500-600 soldiers.

verses.zh: 他们给他脱了衣服，穿上一件朱红色袍子，
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] stripped him and put a scarlet robe[NOTE:2] around him,
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

The scarlet robe probably refers to a military garment that was cheaply dyed in contrast to expensive royal purple, but it resembled a king’s robe (BDAG 554 s.v. κόκκινος). The soldiers did this to Jesus as a form of mockery in view of the charges that he was a king.

verses.zh: 用荆棘编做冠冕，戴在他头上，拿一根苇子放在他右手里，跪在他面前，戏弄他，说：「恭喜，犹太人的王啊！」
verses.en: and after braiding[NOTE:1] a crown of thorns,[NOTE:2] they put it on his head. They[NOTE:3] put a staff[NOTE:4] in his right hand, and kneeling down before him, they mocked him:[NOTE:5] “Hail, king of the Jews!”[NOTE:6]
notes: Or “weaving.”

The crown may have been made from palm spines or some other thorny plant common in Israel. In placing the crown of thorns on his head, the soldiers were unwittingly symbolizing God’s curse on humanity (cf. Gen 3:18) being placed on Jesus. Their purpose would have been to mock Jesus’ claim to be a king; the crown of thorns would have represented the “radiant corona” portrayed on the heads of rulers on coins and other artifacts in the 1st century.
Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Or “a reed.” The Greek term can mean either “staff” or “reed.” See BDAG 502 s.v. κάλαμος 2.
Grk “they mocked him, saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant and has not been translated.
The statement Hail, King of the Jews! is a mockery patterned after the Romans’ cry of Ave, Caesar (“Hail, Caesar!”).tn Or “Long live the King of the Jews!”

verses.zh: 又吐唾沫在他脸上，拿苇子打他的头。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] spat on him and took the staff[NOTE:2] and struck him repeatedly[NOTE:3] on the head.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Or “the reed.”
The verb here has been translated as an iterative imperfect.

verses.zh: 戏弄完了，就给他脱了袍子，仍穿上他自己的衣服，带他出去，要钉十字架。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] they had mocked him, they stripped him of the robe and put his own clothes back on him. Then[NOTE:2] they led him away to crucify him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 他们出来的时候，遇见一个古利奈人，名叫西门，就勉强他同去，好背着耶稣的十字架。
verses.en: As[NOTE:1] they were going out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon, whom they forced[NOTE:2] to carry his cross.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Or “conscripted”; or “pressed into service.”

Jesus was beaten severely with a whip before this (the prelude to crucifixion, known to the Romans as verberatio, mentioned in Matt 27:26; Mark 15:15; John 19:1), so he would have been weak from trauma and loss of blood. Apparently he was unable to bear the cross himself, so Simon was conscripted to help (in all probability this was only the crossbeam, called in Latin the patibulum, since the upright beam usually remained in the ground at the place of execution). Cyrene was located in North Africa where Tripoli is today. Nothing more is known about this Simon. Mark 15:21 names him as father of two people apparently known to Mark’s audience.

verses.zh: 到了一个地方名叫各各他，意思就是「髑髅地」。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] came to a place called Golgotha[NOTE:2] (which means “Place of the Skull”)[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
This is an Aramaic name; see John 19:17.

A place called Golgotha (which means “Place of the Skull”). This location is north and just outside of Jerusalem. The hill on which it is located protruded much like a skull, giving the place its name. The Latin word for the Greek term κρανίον (kranion) is calvaria, from which the English word “Calvary” is derived (cf. Luke 23:33 in the KJV).

verses.zh: 兵丁拿苦胆调和的酒给耶稣喝。他尝了，就不肯喝。
verses.en: and offered Jesus[NOTE:1] wine mixed with gall to drink.[NOTE:2] But after tasting it, he would not drink it.
notes: Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

It is difficult to say for certain who gave Jesus this drink of wine mixed with gall (e.g., the executioner, or perhaps women from Jerusalem). In any case, whoever gave it to him most likely did so in order to relieve his pain, but Jesus was unwilling to take it.

verses.zh: 他们既将他钉在十字架上，就拈阄分他的衣服，
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] they had crucified[NOTE:2] him, they divided his clothes by throwing dice.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
See the note on crucified in 20:19.

An allusion to Ps 22:18.tn Grk “by throwing the lot” (probably by using marked pebbles or broken pieces of pottery). A modern equivalent, “throwing dice,” was chosen here because of its association with gambling. According to L&N 6.219 a term for “dice” is particularly appropriate.

verses.zh: 又坐在那里看守他。
verses.en: Then they sat down and kept guard over him there.

verses.zh: 在他头以上安一个牌子，写着他的罪状，说：「这是犹太人的王耶稣。」
verses.en: Above[NOTE:1] his head they put the charge against him,[NOTE:2] which read:[NOTE:3] “This is Jesus, the king of the Jews.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

Mention of the inscription is an important detail because the inscription would normally give the reason for the execution. It shows that Jesus was executed for claiming to be a king. It was also probably written with irony from the executioners’ point of view.
Grk “was written.”

verses.zh: 当时，有两个强盗和他同钉十字架，一个在右边，一个在左边。
verses.en: Then two outlaws were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.

verses.zh: 从那里经过的人讥诮他，摇着头，说：
verses.en: Those[NOTE:1] who passed by defamed him, shaking their heads
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 「你这拆毁圣殿、三日又建造起来的，可以救自己吧！你如果是　神的儿子，就从十字架上下来吧！」
verses.en: and saying, “You who can destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself![NOTE:1] If you are God’s Son, come down[NOTE:2] from the cross!”
notes: There is rich irony in the statements of those who were passing by, “save yourself!” and “come down from the cross!” In summary, they wanted Jesus to come down from the cross and save his physical life, but it was indeed his staying on the cross and giving his physical life that led to the fact that they could experience a resurrection from death to life.

‡ Many significant witnesses (א* A D it sy[s],p) read καί (kai, here with the force of “then”) before κατάβηθι (katabēthi, “come down”). The shorter reading may well be due to homoioarcton, but judging by the diverse external evidence (א2 B L W Γ Δ Θ 0250 ƒ1,13 33 565 579 700 1241 1424 M lat) it is equally possible that the shorter reading is the wording of the initial text (and is so considered for this translation). NA28 puts the καί in brackets, indicating doubts as to its authenticity.

verses.zh: 祭司长和文士并长老也是这样戏弄他，说：
verses.en: In[NOTE:1] the same way even the chief priests—together with the experts in the law[NOTE:2] and elders[NOTE:3]—were mocking him:[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Or “with the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 2:4.
Only “chief priests” is in the nominative case; this sentence structure attempts to capture this emphasis.
Grk “Mocking him, the chief priests…said.”

verses.zh: 「他救了别人，不能救自己。他是以色列的王，现在可以从十字架上下来，我们就信他。
verses.en: “He saved others, but he cannot save himself! He is the king of Israel! If he comes down[NOTE:1] now from the cross, we will believe in him!
notes: Here the aorist imperative καταβάτω (katabatō) has been translated as a conditional imperative. This fits the pattern of other conditional imperatives (imperative + καί + future indicative) outlined by ExSyn 489.

verses.zh: 他倚靠　神，　神若喜悦他，现在可以救他；因为他曾说：『我是　神的儿子。』」
verses.en: He trusts in God—let God, if he wants to, deliver him now[NOTE:1] because he said, ‘I am God’s Son’!”
notes: An allusion to Ps 22:8.

verses.zh: 那和他同钉的强盗也是这样地讥诮他。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] robbers who were crucified with him also spoke abusively to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Matthew’s wording suggests that both of the criminals spoke abusively to him. If so, one of them quickly changed his attitude toward Jesus (see Luke 23:40-43).

verses.zh: 从午正到申初，遍地都黑暗了。
verses.en: Now from noon until three,[NOTE:1] darkness came over all the land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “from the sixth hour to the ninth hour.”
This imagery has parallels to the Day of the Lord: Joel 2:10; Amos 8:9; Zeph 1:15.

verses.zh: 约在申初，耶稣大声喊着说：「以利！以利！拉马撒巴各大尼？」就是说：「我的　神！我的　神！为甚么离弃我？」
verses.en: At[NOTE:1] about three o’clock Jesus shouted with a loud voice,[NOTE:2] “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “with a loud voice, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant here in contemporary English and has not been translated.
A quotation from Ps 22:1.

verses.zh: 站在那里的人，有的听见就说：「这个人呼叫以利亚呢！」
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] some of the bystanders heard it, they said, “This man is calling for Elijah.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 内中有一个人赶紧跑去，拿海绒蘸满了醋，绑在苇子上，送给他喝。
verses.en: Immediately[NOTE:1] one of them ran and got a sponge, filled it with sour wine,[NOTE:2] put it on a stick,[NOTE:3] and gave it to him to drink.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

Sour wine refers to cheap wine that was called in Latin posca, a cheap vinegar wine diluted heavily with water. It was the drink of slaves and soldiers, and was probably there for the soldiers who had performed the crucifixion.
Grk “a reed.”

verses.zh: 其余的人说：「且等着，看以利亚来救他不来。」
verses.en: But the rest said, “Leave him alone! Let’s see if Elijah will come to save him.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Early and significant witnesses, including the chief Alexandrian mss (א B C L Γ 1010 and some versional witnesses) add a sentence at the end of this verse: “And another [soldier] took a spear and pierced him in the side, and water and blood flowed out.” This comment finds such a strong parallel in John 19:34 that it was undoubtedly lifted from the Fourth Gospel by some early, well-meaning scribe and inserted into Matt 27:49. The alternative—that this sentence was part of Matthew’s Ausgangstext—has serious difficulties, as Metzger notes: “It might be thought that the words were omitted because they represent the piercing as preceding Jesus’ death, whereas John makes it follow; but that difference would have only been a reason for moving the passage to a later position (perhaps at the close of ver. 50 or 54 or 56), or else there would have been some tampering with the passage in John, which is not the case. It is probable that the Johannine passage was written by some reader in the margin of Matthew from memory (there are several minor differences, such as the sequence of ‘water and blood’), and a later copyist awkwardly introduced it into the text” (TCGNT, 59). Consequently, even though the support for the shorter reading (A D W Θ ƒ1,13 33 565 579 700 1241 1424 M lat sy sa bo) is not as impressive, internal considerations on its behalf are compelling.

verses.zh: 耶稣又大声喊叫，气就断了。
verses.en: Then Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and gave up his spirit.

verses.zh: 忽然，殿里的幔子从上到下裂为两半，地也震动，磐石也崩裂，
verses.en: Just then[NOTE:1] the temple curtain[NOTE:2] was torn in two, from top to bottom. The[NOTE:3] earth shook and the rocks were split apart.
notes: Grk “And behold.”

The referent of this term, καταπέτασμα (katapetasma), is not entirely clear. It could refer to the curtain separating the holy of holies from the holy place (Josephus, J. W. 5.5.5 [5.219]), or it could refer to one at the entrance of the temple court (Josephus, J. W. 5.5.4 [5.212]). Many argue that the inner curtain is meant because another term, κάλυμμα (kalumma), is also used for the outer curtain. Others see a reference to the outer curtain as more likely because of the public nature of this sign. Either way, the symbolism means that access to God has been opened up.
Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 坟墓也开了，已睡圣徒的身体多有起来的。
verses.en: And tombs were opened, and the bodies of many saints who had died[NOTE:1] were raised.
notes: The verb κοιμάω (koimaō) literally means “sleep,” but it is often used in the Bible as a euphemism for the death of a believer.

verses.zh: 到耶稣复活以后，他们从坟墓里出来，进了圣城，向许多人显现。
verses.en: (They[NOTE:1] came out of the tombs after his resurrection and went into the holy city and appeared to many people.)
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 百夫长和一同看守耶稣的人看见地震并所经历的事，就极其害怕，说：「这真是　神的儿子了！」
verses.en: Now when the centurion[NOTE:1] and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what took place, they were extremely terrified and said, “Truly this one was God’s Son!”
notes: See the note on the word centurion in Matt 8:5.

verses.zh: 有好些妇女在那里，远远地观看；她们是从加利利跟随耶稣来服事他的。
verses.en: Many[NOTE:1] women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and given him support[NOTE:2] were also there, watching from a distance.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “and ministered to him.”sn Cf. Luke 8:3.

verses.zh: 内中有抹大拉的马利亚，又有雅各和约西的母亲马利亚，并有西庇太两个儿子的母亲。
verses.en: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

verses.zh: 到了晚上，有一个财主，名叫约瑟，是亚利马太来的，他也是耶稣的门徒。
verses.en: Now when it was evening, there came a rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph, who was also a disciple of Jesus.[NOTE:1]
notes: Though some dispute that Joseph of Arimathea was a disciple of Jesus, his actions regarding Jesus’ burial suggest otherwise.

verses.zh: 这人去见彼拉多，求耶稣的身体；彼拉多就吩咐给他。
verses.en: He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.[NOTE:1] Then Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
notes: Asking for the body of Jesus was indeed a bold move on the part of Joseph of Arimathea, for it clearly and openly identified him with a man who had just been condemned and executed, namely, Jesus. His faith is exemplary, especially for someone who was a member of the council that handed Jesus over for crucifixion (cf. Mark 15:43, Luke 23:51). He did this because he sought to give Jesus an honorable burial.

verses.zh: 约瑟取了身体，用干净细麻布裹好，
verses.en: Joseph[NOTE:1] took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
The term σινδών (sindōn) can refer to a linen cloth used either for clothing or for burial.

verses.zh: 安放在自己的新坟墓里，就是他凿在磐石里的。他又把大石头滚到墓门口，就去了。
verses.en: and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut in the rock.[NOTE:1] Then he rolled a great stone across the entrance[NOTE:2] of the tomb and went away.
notes: That is, cut or carved into an outcropping of natural rock, resulting in a cave-like structure (see L&N 19.25).
Or “to the door,” “against the door.”

verses.zh: 有抹大拉的马利亚和那个马利亚在那里，对着坟墓坐着。
verses.en: (Now Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there, opposite the tomb.)

verses.zh: 次日，就是预备日的第二天，祭司长和法利赛人聚集来见彼拉多，说：
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] next day (which is after the day of preparation) the chief priests and the Pharisees[NOTE:2] assembled before Pilate
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
See the note on Pharisees in 3:7.

verses.zh: 「大人，我们记得那诱惑人的还活着的时候曾说：『三日后我要复活。』
verses.en: and said, “Sir, we remember that while that deceiver was still alive he said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’

verses.zh: 因此，请吩咐人将坟墓把守妥当，直到第三日，恐怕他的门徒来，把他偷了去，就告诉百姓说：『他从死里复活了。』这样，那后来的迷惑比先前的更利害了！」
verses.en: So give orders to secure the tomb until the third day. Otherwise his disciples may come and steal his body[NOTE:1] and say to the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead,’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
notes: Grk “him.”

verses.zh: 彼拉多说：「你们有看守的兵，去吧！尽你们所能的把守妥当。」
verses.en: Pilate said to them, “Take[NOTE:1] a guard of soldiers. Go and make it as secure as you can.”
notes: Grk “You have a guard.”

verses.zh: 他们就带着看守的兵同去，封了石头，将坟墓把守妥当。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they went with the soldiers[NOTE:2] of the guard and made the tomb secure by sealing the stone.
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of Pilate’s order.
Grk “with the guard.” The words “soldiers of the” have been supplied in the translation to prevent “guard” from being misunderstood as a single individual.
